findings.title: Targets are now interpolated twice (runSplitQuery + DataSourceWithBackend.query)
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now maps every target through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`, but each sub-request is later executed with `datasource.runQuery(subRequest)`, which goes through `DataSourceWithBackend.query()` and applies `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again to the same (already interpolated) target. The second pass is not a no-op: Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` calls `addAdHocFilters(target.expr, adhocFilters)`, so ad-hoc filters are injected into the expression a second time (duplicated label matchers / duplicated `| key="value"` stages), and `templateSrv.replace` runs again over the already-substituted expression, so a variable value that itself contains a `$`-prefixed token gets expanded a second time. It also costs an extra LogQL parse/rewrite per sub-request. Either the pre-interpolation needs a way to mark targets as already interpolated, or the interpolation must stay in a single place.

findings.title: Shard path interpolates, then delegates to runSplitQuery which interpolates again
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates all targets here, builds a sub-request whose expressions already contain the shard matcher (`__stream_shard__=~"..."` / `| drop __stream_shard__`), and then passes it to `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which — after this PR — interpolates every target once more, and `datasource.runQuery` triggers a third pass inside `DataSourceWithBackend.query`. The repeated `applyTemplateVariables` calls re-run `addAdHocFilters` on the shard-rewritten expression, so ad-hoc filters can be added two or three times (duplicated matchers, and for non-indexed labels filter stages appended after the injected `drop` stage). The updated test at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 (`applyTemplateVariables` expected to be called 5 times for one target) is direct evidence of this redundancy; it only passes because the mock returns the same object unchanged after the first call.

findings.title: New interpolation test mocks replace() so it cannot show $__auto is actually resolved up-front
findings.body: The test supplies a `replace` implementation that unconditionally rewrites `$__auto` and `$step` regardless of the `scopedVars` it is given. Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` deliberately strips `__auto`/`__interval`/`__interval_ms`/`__range*` from `scopedVars` because those are interpolated on the backend, so in production `$__auto` will still be present in the expression after this new front-end interpolation step and will be resolved per sub-request range on the backend — i.e. the behaviour the linked issue complains about. With the current mock the assertion on `count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])` passes no matter what `applyTemplateVariables` does with `$__auto`, giving false confidence that the issue is fixed. The test should drive interpolation through realistic `scopedVars` (including `__auto`) and a `replace` that honours them.

findings.title: Test asserts a magic call count that encodes redundant interpolation, and the mutating mock hides repeat interpolation
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` locks in the fact that one target is interpolated once in `runShardSplitQuery` plus once per sub-request inside `runSplitQuery`. Because the mock mutates and returns the same query object (`query.expr = query.expr.replace('$SELECTOR', ...)`), the extra calls are no-ops and the test cannot detect side effects of repeated interpolation such as duplicated ad-hoc filters. Any future change to the number of shard groups will also break this assertion for reasons unrelated to interpolation. A test asserting that ad-hoc filters/variables are applied exactly once to the final expression would be more meaningful.
